questions.question_text: The parabola $y=x^2-2x+c$ has one $x$-intercept at $x=5$. Find $c$, the other $x$-intercept and the vertex.

options.why: Dropped the negative when solving $25-10+c=0$, flipping the sign of $c$.
Found the other intercept by symmetry with the wrong axis distance.
Used $x=+\dfrac{b}{2a}$, giving the wrong axis for the vertex.

questions.solution_text:
Since $x=5$ is an $x$-intercept, substitute $x=5$, $y=0$.
$0=(5)^2-2(5)+c$
$0=15+c$
$c=-15$
So $y=x^2-2x-15=(x-5)(x+3)$, giving the other $x$-intercept $x=-3$.
Axis of symmetry: $x=-\dfrac{-2}{2(1)}=1$, and $y=(1)^2-2(1)-15=-16$.
The vertex is $(1,-16)$.
